editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the stochastic SabreSwap caveats, the optimization-level pass lists and the Scheduling stage, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The main problem is that "circuit" is rendered three ways: mostly "Circuit", but also "Quantenschaltkreis(e)" in [20], [46] and [48], and "Quantum-Circuit"/"Quantum-Gates" in [0] and [39]. "Optimization Level 1" stays in English in [26] but becomes "Optimierungslevel" in [27] and [48]. Smaller points: [22] drops the "tries to" hedge for the heuristic pass, [23] calques "historical behavior", and the defaults page title is rendered two different ways in [14] and [71].

examples.source: When writing a quantum circuit, you are free to use any quantum gate
examples.translation: Beim Schreiben eines Quantum-Circuits kannst du beliebige Quantum-Gates
examples.suggested: Beim Schreiben eines Quantum-Circuits kannst du beliebige Gates
examples.why: Hybrid 'Quantum-Circuit'/'Quantum-Gates' sits alongside 'Quantenschaltkreis' ([20], [46], [48]) and plain 'Circuit' (elsewhere). The page should pick one rendering, and plain 'Circuit' is the dominant one.
The rest of the page says 'Optimierungslevel' ([27], [48], [58]), so this English leftover is inconsistent.

examples.source: a heuristic pass that tries to find the best layout to use if a perfect layout cannot be found
examples.translation: ein heuristischer Pass eingesetzt, der das beste Layout ermittelt, falls kein perfektes Layout gefunden werden kann
examples.suggested: ein heuristischer Pass eingesetzt, der versucht, das beste Layout zu finden, falls kein perfektes Layout gefunden werden kann
examples.why: Dropping 'tries to' slightly overstates what a heuristic guarantees. The page itself says the heuristic result is good but not necessarily optimal ([30]).

examples.source: This is historical behavior only used in `optimzation_level=1`
examples.translation: Dies ist ein historisches Verhalten, das nur bei `optimzation_level=1` verwendet wird
examples.suggested: Dieses Verhalten ist historisch bedingt und wird nur bei `optimzation_level=1` verwendet
examples.why: 'ein historisches Verhalten' is a calque; a German technical writer would say 'historisch bedingt' or use 'Legacy-Verhalten'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. Density matrices, channels, measurements and the Credly and badge passages are rendered accurately, and the "du" register holds. The one defect is a case error in entry [0]: "einschließlich Dichtematrizen, Kanäle und allgemeine Messungen" uses the nominative after "einschließlich". The correct form is genitive "allgemeiner Messungen" or, because the article-less plurals do not show the genitive, dative "Kanälen und allgemeinen Messungen".

examples.source: Dive deeper into quantum information, including density matrices, channels, and general measurements.
examples.translation: Tauche tiefer in die Quanteninformation ein, einschließlich Dichtematrizen, Kanäle und allgemeine Messungen.
examples.suggested: Tauche tiefer in die Quanteninformation ein – mit Dichtematrizen, Kanälen und allgemeinen Messungen.
examples.why: "einschließlich" takes the genitive, or the dative when the plural noun has no article. The nominative "Kanäle und allgemeine Messungen" is a grammar error a native editor would fix.

editor_note: The translation is mostly faithful and reads naturally, but entry [177] reverses the purpose of a step. The English says we choose an initial point suited to the Hamiltonian. The German says "wir verwenden den passenden Startpunkt, um den Hamiltonoperator anzupassen", which tells the learner the starting point is used to modify the Hamiltonian. In [132], "expected values" became "bekannten Erwartungswerten", which collides with the quantum-mechanical term Erwartungswert (expectation value). The remaining issues are minor inconsistencies: Hamiltonoperator / Hamilton-Operator / bare "Hamiltonian" ([164]-[166], [175]); Testwellenfunktion vs. Versuchs-Wellenfunktion ([207], [216]); and the "Check your understanding" heading rendered three ways (Verständnisfragen / Verständnistest / Verständnis überprüfen).

examples.source: we will use the appropriate initial point to fit the Hamiltonian
examples.translation: wir verwenden den passenden Startpunkt, um den Hamiltonoperator anzupassen
examples.suggested: wir verwenden einen zum Hamiltonoperator passenden Startpunkt
examples.why: The German says the starting point is used to modify the Hamiltonian, which is a false picture of what VQE does. The Hamiltonian is fixed; only the initial parameters are chosen to suit it.

examples.source: compare our calculated ground state energy to expected values
examples.why: Erwartungswert is the technical term for an expectation value (<H>), which the same page uses in [133]. Here the English only means reference values, so the German wording invites confusion.

examples.source: used by the previous VQE and Hamiltonian
examples.translation: vom vorherigen VQE und Hamiltonian verwendet
examples.suggested: vom vorherigen VQE und Hamiltonoperator verwendet
examples.why: English 'Hamiltonian' is left untranslated here. The rest of the file uses Hamiltonoperator, and [164]-[166] use Hamilton-Operator, so the term appears in three forms.
Earlier entries ([24], [30], [133]) render 'trial wave function' as Testwellenfunktion, but [207], [216] and [219] switch to Versuchs-.
The same recurring heading is rendered as Verständnisfragen, Verständnistest and Verständnis überprüfen ([181]). It should use one form throughout.

examples.source: we will actually calculate this value in the check-in problem
examples.translation: wir werden diesen Wert tatsächlich in der Check-in-Aufgabe berechnen
examples.suggested: diesen Wert berechnen wir selbst in der folgenden Verständnisfrage
examples.why: 'Check-in-Aufgabe' is an anglicism, and 'tatsächlich' is a calque of 'actually'. Elsewhere the file says Verständnisfrage.
